DirectTransfer_HeartTimeMixer.critical_finding: PREDICTION COLLAPSE, not pure domain shift. pred_mean ~74.7 for ALL targets (BGT60 true=83.6). Per-participant pred spread <0.3 BPM while true HR spans 57.6-88.0. In-domain Pearson ~0. Train MAE stuck at ~9.4 (== predict-the-mean) -> model never fits training set.
DirectTransfer_HeartTimeMixer.diagnostic_ridge: Ridge regression on same x_time+x_freq features: MAE=8.65, Pearson r=0.34, pred span 57-90 BPM. => features DO carry modest HR signal; HeartTimeMixer training is broken (collapses below even a linear baseline).
DirectTransfer_HeartTimeMixer.implication: Do NOT evaluate DANN/CORAL/WPL on top of a base model that cannot learn HR in-domain. Fix/verify base model first.

diagnostic_chain.ridge_on_same_features: in-sample MAE=8.65, Pearson r=0.34, pred span 57-90 BPM => features carry MODEST HR signal
diagnostic_chain.TCN_ftu_test: MAE=4.67, r=-0.066, pred_mean=73.15 => TCN ALSO collapses (not HTM-specific)
diagnostic_chain.overfit_2batches_default_lr: 60 epochs on 2 batches, train MAE still 8.556 => cannot even memorize training data
diagnostic_chain.overfit_2batches_lr_1e-2: train MAE 9.073 => raising lr does NOT help => structural/forward bug, not lr
diagnostic_chain.output_variance_test: 5 inputs with labels 73-86 BPM -> predictions 74.7-76.2 (std 0.57) => model nearly input-independent

DirectTransfer_HeartTimeMixer.conclusion: Deep-model training/forward is broken (collapse); features are only weakly informative (linear ceiling r~0.34). Cross-domain premise CANNOT be tested until base model learns HR in-domain. Priority pivot: fix base model before DANN/CORAL/WPL.

notes: Direct Transfer = train on FTU, evaluate on target test split with source label_stats. RMSE/Pearson added to evaluate_model.py. by_dataset/by_participant saved in eval JSONs. Provenance saved in run_config.json + eval JSON.
